small_guidance:
- The inner-most loop reloads the same `x` tile for every `oc_start` iteration; swap the loop order so `k_start` is the outer loop and accumulate min across `oc_start` inside, OR (better) make BLOCK_M cover all of OC (OC=128) in a single pass so the x-gather happens once per spatial tile. Add an autotune config with `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=16/32` that matches OC exactly.
- Add larger spatial tiles (`BLOCK_N=128`) and try `BLOCK_K=64` with `num_warps=8, num_stages=2`; current best config likely under-utilizes since output spatial is 254*254≈64k per batch and grid only parallelizes across batches × spatial tiles.
- Persist `min_val` register across the K-loop only, and replace the per-tile `tl.where(oc_mask, ..., inf)` masking with bounding `BLOCK_M` to a multiple of OC at autotune time to avoid the extra select.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as one program per (N, output-spatial tile) with a single pass over OC: since OC=128 is small, hold the full `[OC, BLOCK_N]` accumulator in registers/SMEM and stream the K=IC*KH*KW dimension once. This eliminates redundant x-gathers across oc tiles (currently x is re-fetched ⌈OC/BLOCK_M⌉ times per spatial tile) and lets the channel-min reduction happen at the end without writing the full conv output.
- Switch input layout to NHWC (channels_last) so the K-dim (ic) is contiguous and the implicit-im2col gather coalesces; the current NCHW layout makes the x-load strided over ic.
- Consider a 2D output-spatial tile (e.g. 8×32) instead of a flat 1D BLOCK_N — neighboring output pixels share most of the KH×KW input window, enabling reuse of x loads through register tiling and dropping HBM traffic by ~KH·KW× along the shared dimension.
